Pagefeather

WordPress and WooCommerce on Cloudflare, in your own Cloudflare account.

Build WordPress sites without looking after a WordPress server. You deploy into the Cloudflare account you already own. There is no hosted funnel and no upsell.

Get started
Read the limits
GitHub

Two ways to run a site

Built-in database

b-dosql. PHP and SQLite live in one Durable Object. You need no MySQL server.

  • WordPress on Workers Free or Workers Paid
  • A light WooCommerce storefront
  • One writer, one region per site
  • About 5 uncached requests a second

MySQL option

Approach A. PHP runs in a Worker. MySQL sits outside Cloudflare. Hyperdrive holds the pool.

  • Workers Paid required
  • Path for a real WooCommerce store
  • Scales out across isolates
  • You also pay for the MySQL server

Many sites on one account use Workers for Platforms at $30 a month for two or more sites. See cost.

How it works
See a live store

What is solid today

Cached guest reads ran about 26 to 30 requests a second per site in our load test, with a p50 near 200 ms. That figure is a lower bound set by the test client (docs/load-152.md, 2026-11-08).

  • Logged-out guest pages can come from the edge page cache and never reach PHP.
  • Approach A: WordPress wp suite 18 of 18, and routes.py with 0 failures, on site cf759hw (results.md, 2026-11-20).
  • Approach A: WooCommerce tests/woo.py 12 of 12, three runs in a row (results.md, 2026-11-09).
  • Fresh-clone deploys for b-dosql, Workers for Platforms, and approach A Pass from a clean clone (results.md, 2026-11-24).

Where it stops

  • WooCommerce on b-dosql is a light storefront. A real store uses approach A (#1022).
  • On b-dosql under load, the Durable Object isolate can reset and lose writes. We measured 43 resets and 49 lost writes per 1000 server requests on cf759a (2026-11-22).
  • Editing a WooCommerce store on Workers Free does not fit Free memory (#638).
  • Approach A cold isolates cost 3 to 9 s more on the first request (#1169).
  • Full open list: Limits and docs/guide/limits.md.

This site

www.pagefeather.dev is itself a b-dosql WordPress deploy on Workers Paid (MEDIA=1, WooCommerce off). It is a living example of the built-in database path, not a hosted product.

The project is young. Some parts are measured and solid. Some are still being built. Read the limits before you build on it.
